about.en:
The Bachelor Students' Targeted Grant competition (BSG) is run by the Shota Rustaveli National Science Foundation, Georgia's main public research funder. It aims to spark scientific interest among undergraduates, reward innovative ideas and build research capacity early.

Projects are institutional: a team of at least three active bachelor students (Georgian citizens enrolled in accredited programmes in Georgia) forms the core staff, with a project leader and a lead organisation such as a university or research institute. The Foundation funds up to 15,000 GEL per project.

Registration is electronic in the Foundation's Gmus system (30 Oct - 13 Nov 2026), followed by a paper declaration at the Foundation's office by 17 November. Online group consultations are held on 3 and 10 November. Evaluation and results follow in December 2026.

en: Up to 15,000 GEL for a student-led research project
Real experience writing and managing a national research grant
Free online consultations on 3 and 10 November 2026

eligibility.en: Active bachelor students who are citizens of Georgia and enrolled in an accredited bachelor programme at a higher education institution registered in Georgia. Minimum team of three, plus a lead organisation (public or non-profit legal entity, e.g. a university).

en: Form a team of at least three bachelor students and agree a project leader
Secure a lead organisation (usually your university) to host the project
Register the project in Gmus (gmus.rustaveli.org.ge) by 13 Nov 2026 18:00
Submit the signed participation declaration to the Foundation by 17 Nov 2026 18:00
Join the online consultations (3 and 10 Nov) if you have questions

costs.en: No application fee. Grant of up to 15,000 GEL per project.

about.en:
"Leonardo da Vinci" is the Rustaveli Foundation's flagship competition for young inventors and researchers in Georgian schools. It encourages interest in science, technology and creative problem-solving.

Students in grades VII-XII of any public or private school in Georgia can enter individually or in groups of up to three. In the first stage they submit a written project in the Gmus system; shortlisted entrants then submit a drawing, model or prototype in the second stage, and finalists present at a competition exhibition where winners are chosen and awarded.

The 2026 cycle opened on 16 March with consultations in March-April; expect the 2027 call around March 2027 on the Foundation's 'current competitions' page.

Open to individual students or teams of up to three
Builds a strong science/engineering portfolio for university applications

eligibility.en: Students in grades VII-XII of general education schools (public or private) in Georgia. Individuals or groups of up to three students.

en: Watch the Foundation's current competitions page from March 2027
Prepare a project idea (invention or research) with a supervising teacher if possible
Register the first-stage application in Gmus
If shortlisted, submit your model/drawing/prototype for the second stage
Present at the final exhibition

costs.en: Free to enter. Prizes for winners are paid by the Foundation.

about.en:
Market Hack is a 36-hour hackathon organised by Georgia's Innovation and Technology Agency (GITA) at its Gurjaani Technopark in Kakheti. Participants tackle real marketing-sector challenges with technology and fresh approaches, and can turn ideas into prototypes using the technopark's FabLab and mentor support.

It is open to participants from all over Georgia aged 16 and over, individually or in teams of 2-4. Round-trip transport between Tbilisi and Gurjaani is provided. The author(s) of the best project receive a 10,000 GEL grant to develop the prototype.

Register through the GITA form linked on the programme page; contact: egogolashvili@gita.gov.ge.

Re:Start - Re:Vive is a week-long STEAM programme at GITA's Ozurgeti Technopark (Guria). Instead of starting from scratch, participants revisit, improve and develop ideas from earlier projects and hackathons, working on real problems and producing 10-12 technological prototypes by the end of the week.

This GITA workshop at Gurjaani Technopark introduces robotics with LEGO Education SPIKE. Participants assemble mechanisms from LEGO parts, work with sensors and motors, learn the basics of block-based programming and create interactive robots that complete tasks.

It focuses on logical thinking, problem-solving and creativity, using a learning-by-doing approach. Free for ages 10+.

Create interactive robots
Free

GITA's Gurjaani Technopark hosts a Tech Talk with Giorgi Danelia, a Georgian video-blogger and businessman who founded GD Squad and GD Tech. The talk covers modern technologies and their practical use, development trends, marketing and digital content creation.

It is open to school students aged 15+, university students and anyone interested in tech, marketing and content creation. Only the first 90 registered participants can attend.

Learn about content creation and tech marketing
Free, 15+

summary.en: A case competition in which university teams analyse a real dilemma faced by the National Bank of Georgia and present policy recommendations to central bankers. Prizes are 4,000, 2,000 and 1,500 GEL for the top three teams.
summary.ka: ქეის-კონკურსი, რომელშიც სტუდენტური გუნდები საქართველოს ეროვნული ბანკის რეალურ დილემას აანალიზებენ და რეკომენდაციებს ცენტრალური ბანკის ჟიურის წარუდგენენ. პრიზები: 4 000, 2 000 და 1 500 ლარი პირველი სამი გუნდისთვის.
summary.ar: مسابقة حالات دراسية تحلل فيها فرق جامعية معضلة حقيقية يواجهها البنك الوطني الجورجي وتقدّم توصيات إلى لجنة من مسؤولي البنك. الجوائز 4,000 و2,000 و1,500 لاري للفرق الثلاثة الأولى.

about.en:
"Regulator's Dilemma" is the National Bank of Georgia's annual student competition, run through its FINEDU financial-education platform with support from Credo Bank. Teams receive a real dilemma from central-bank work, analyse it and present practical recommendations to a jury of at least three NBG experts.

Teams of 3-6 bachelor or master students from the same authorised Georgian university register online; only the first 20 teams get into round one. Five teams reach the final round and three winners share prizes of 4,000, 2,000 and 1,500 GEL (split among members). In 2026 registration was 19-25 October, round one 16-17 November and the final on 7 December.

It is an excellent way for economics, finance and law students to understand monetary policy and supervision and to get noticed by the central bank.

en: Work on a real central-bank policy dilemma
Present to NBG experts; prizes up to 4,000 GEL
Strong CV signal for economics/finance careers

eligibility.en: Teams of 3-6 students enrolled in bachelor or master programmes at the same authorised higher education institution in Georgia (members may be from different years and faculties). Working language Georgian.

en: Watch finedu.gov.ge events in early October 2027 for the call
Form a team of 3-6 students from your university
Register via the online form as soon as registration opens (first 20 teams only)
Solve the first-round assignment and email it to info@finedu.gov.ge
Present to the jury; finalists get a second assignment

score_reason: Prestigious annual case competition; 2027 dates estimated

summary.ar: مسابقة رسم للأطفال من 6 إلى 17 عامًا ينظمها البنك الوطني الجورجي كل مارس ضمن أسبوع المال العالمي. في 2026 صمّم المشاركون ورقة نقدية لمنطقتهم، وحصل سبعة فائزين على 500 لاري لكل منهم.

about.en:
Every March, the National Bank of Georgia's FINEDU platform celebrates Global Money Week with creative competitions for children. In 2026 the theme was "My Region - My Banknote": entrants hand-drew both sides of a banknote representing their city, village or region, including security features such as a serial number and security thread.

It is open to children and teens aged 6-17 in three age groups (6-9, 10-13, 14-17). Entries are posted as a comment on FINEDU's official Facebook competition post (parents submit for under-16s). A jury from the NBG and partner banks picks two winners per age group, plus a public-vote winner; each received 500 GEL plus educational gifts.

The theme changes each year, so check finedu.gov.ge in March 2027.

en: Cash prizes (500 GEL per winner in 2026)
Three age groups from 6 to 17
Fun way to learn about money and banknotes

eligibility.en: Children and teenagers aged 6-17 (2026 rules). Prizes are paid into a bank account in Georgia. Entries in Georgian context.

en: Check finedu.gov.ge events in March 2027 for the theme and rules
Create a hand-made artwork (no digital or AI images)
Post a clear photo as a comment on the official FINEDU Facebook competition post with name and age (parent submits for under-16s)

costs.en: Free. Prizes paid by the National Bank of Georgia and partner banks.

score_reason: Easy, free, annual national competition for younger students

about.en:
The Georgian National Museum, which unites Georgia's main museums (including the Simon Janashia Museum on Rustaveli Avenue), runs a volunteer programme to help people build professional skills in museum work. Volunteers name the department or unit they want to work in, so it suits students of history, archaeology, art, conservation, education or communications.

The museum looks for motivation, willingness to learn, a general understanding of the museum's work, responsibility and punctuality; computer skills and a foreign language are a plus. A recommendation from a school or workplace helps but is not required.

Apply by submitting the documents to the museum's administrative service; for questions call +995 32 299 80 22.

en: Hands-on experience in Georgia's leading museum
Choose the department you want to work in
Open year-round, any age

eligibility.en: People of various ages with secondary or higher education and an interest in museum work. Foreign language skills are helpful for some projects.

en: Prepare a volunteer application stating the department you want to join
Attach a recommendation (optional), CV, copy of diploma or school certificate, ID copy and two photos
Submit the documents to the museum's administrative service in Tbilisi
Wait to be contacted by the department (call +995 32 299 80 22 for updates)

costs.en: Unpaid volunteering; no fees.

name.ka: უცხოეთში სტაჟირება აჭარელი ახალგაზრდებისთვის (პროგრამა „ევროოდისეა“)

deadline_note: Runs every year since 2006; the ministry announces registration and interview periods on its page. No fixed date published for the next round, so check the page and contact the coordinator.

summary.en: Adjara residents aged 18-35 can win a funded professional internship in a European region through the Eurodyssey exchange of the Assembly of European Regions. Host regions pay a monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR plus a language course, and Adjara adds 2,000 GEL.
summary.ka: აჭარაში რეგისტრირებულ 18-35 წლის ახალგაზრდებს შეუძლიათ ევროპის რეგიონთა ასამბლეის „ევროოდისეას“ პროგრამით ევროპულ რეგიონში დაფინანსებული სტაჟირება მოიპოვონ. მასპინძელი რეგიონი იხდის ყოველთვიურ სტიპენდიას 700-1200 ევროს ოდენობით და ენის კურსს, ხოლო აჭარის სამინისტრო დამატებით 2000 ლარს გასცემს.
summary.ar: يمكن للشباب المسجلين في أجارا (18-35 عامًا) الحصول على تدريب مهني ممول في إقليم أوروبي عبر برنامج يوروديسي التابع لجمعية الأقاليم الأوروبية. يدفع الإقليم المضيف منحة شهرية من 700 إلى 1,200 يورو ودورة لغة، وتضيف وزارة أجارا 2,000 لاري.

about.en:
Since 2006 the Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport has run Georgia's entry into Eurodyssey, the youth exchange programme of the Assembly of European Regions (founded 1985). Participants complete a professional internship in a member region in Europe to build work skills and language ability.

Internships last several months depending on the host region and are fully funded by the host: a monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR covers food and accommodation, and the internship starts with an intensive language course and a cultural programme. AER co-funds insurance; the intern pays travel and visa costs, and after completion the Adjara ministry pays a one-off 2,000 GEL.

Selection has two stages: the ministry's own competition, then registration on eurodyssey.aer.eu and a remote interview with the host region and employer, who make the final decision.

en: Monthly stipend of 700-1,200 EUR paid by the host region
Free intensive language course in the host country
Extra 2,000 GEL from the Adjara ministry after completion

eligibility.en: Citizens of Georgia aged 18-35 registered in the Autonomous Republic of Adjara, with a vocational or higher education diploma and knowledge of a foreign language, who meet the host region's requirements.

en: Read the regulation and document list on the ministry's "Internship abroad" page
Submit the application form and documents to the ministry during the announced registration period
Pass the ministry's first-stage selection
Register your profile on eurodyssey.aer.eu
Interview remotely with the host region and employer

costs.en: Host region pays a 700-1,200 EUR monthly stipend and language course; travel and visa paid by the intern; 2,000 GEL one-off support from Adjara after completion.

score_reason: Funded European internship, but only for Adjara residents

about.en:
The Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport runs a subject olympiad every year under its 'Competitions and Olympiads' subprogramme. Subjects: Georgian language and literature, English and mathematics (grades VII-IX), plus physics, chemistry and biology (grade IX). For Russian-sector pupils, physics, maths, chemistry and biology are held in Russian.

The olympiad is a written test. It is a good warm-up for the national school olympiad and for international olympiads, and past tests are published on the ministry's page.

Past tests published for practice
Stepping stone to national olympiads

Each school can enter one team of five pupils from grades 5-6 and one from grades 7-9 in Georgian language and literature and in mathematics; history and civic education (integrated) is for grades 7-9 teams.

It rewards teamwork and broad knowledge and is a friendly first competition for younger students.

Maths, Georgian, history and civics
Great first competition for younger pupils

Compete on the announced date

It builds exactly the skills needed for scholarship and university applications abroad: academic writing in English, argument and speaking under pressure.

about.en:
The Literary Marathon is part of the Adjara Ministry of Education and Sport's annual olympiads and competitions. Pupils compete in two categories: grades VII-VIII and grades IX-X.

The first round is organised by the ministry and the regional education resource centres; the second is a live written face-off with a host. It suits keen readers who want to test their knowledge of Georgian and world literature.

summary.en: Batumi residents aged 18-29 who are invited to an internship, training, exchange, volunteering or other international project abroad can get up to 3,000 GEL from Batumi City Hall for travel, visa, insurance and fees. Applications are taken every month.
summary.ka: ბათუმში რეგისტრირებულ 18-29 წლის ახალგაზრდებს, რომლებიც უცხოეთში სტაჟირებაზე, ტრენინგზე, გაცვლით, მოხალისეობრივ ან სხვა საერთაშორისო პროექტზე არიან მიწვეულნი, ბათუმის მერია 3 000 ლარამდე უფინანსებს მგზავრობას, ვიზას, დაზღვევასა და საფასურს. განაცხადები ყოველთვიურად მიიღება.
summary.ar: يمكن للشباب المسجلين في باتومي (18-29 عامًا) المدعوين إلى تدريب أو دورة أو تبادل أو تطوع أو مشروع دولي آخر في الخارج الحصول على ما يصل إلى 3,000 لاري من بلدية باتومي لتغطية السفر والتأشيرة والتأمين والرسوم. تُقبل الطلبات كل شهر.

about.en:
Under its 'Professional development support' subprogramme, Batumi City Hall co-funds young people who go abroad for professional internships, practice or retraining, or to take part in educational, cultural, sports, youth, volunteering or other projects (including Erasmus+ youth exchanges and training courses).

Winners receive a one-off grant of up to 3,000 GEL covering travel, visa, insurance and participation or registration fees. Applicants must already hold an invitation and show co-funding (own funds or a sponsor/host). A commission reviews documents and interviews applicants; at least 60% of the maximum score is needed.

Applications are submitted at Batumi City Hall (L. Asatiani St. 25) from the first to the last working day of any month; costs incurred before the contract is signed are not reimbursed. After the trip, you submit a short report and passport stamps.

en: Up to 3,000 GEL for travel, visa, insurance and fees
Covers Erasmus+ projects, internships, volunteering, training abroad
Rolling monthly applications

eligibility.en: Citizens of Georgia aged 18-29 registered in Batumi who have higher or vocational education or are studying at an authorised institution, and who hold an invitation to the project abroad.

en: Get your invitation letter from the host project
Download the regulation, application form and recommendation form from the programme page
Collect documents: ID/passport copy, proof of Batumi registration, recommendation, invitation, 2 photos, proof of co-funding, education certificate (Georgian or notarised translation)
Submit at Batumi City Hall, L. Asatiani St. 25, during any month
Attend the interview and sign the contract before travelling

costs.en: Grant of up to 3,000 GEL (travel, visa, insurance, participation fees). Applicant must show co-funding for the rest.

score_reason: Rolling travel funding that unlocks Erasmus+ and internships abroad for Batumi youth

about.en:
Batumi City Hall's 'Support for Youth Initiatives' (part of the Youth Centre subprogramme) funds outstanding, engaging projects designed by young people themselves. Directions include education and culture, sport and healthy lifestyle, youth policy, and sports/educational tourism (hiking, cycling, rafting, kayaking and similar).

Any individual aged 14-29 registered in Batumi can apply for up to 4,000 GEL per event; the event should normally take place in Batumi within the same budget year. A commission scores applications and the mayor approves winners, after which a contract is signed.

Applications are accepted from the first to the last working day of every month; download the regulation and application form from the programme page.

en: Up to 4,000 GEL for your own youth project
Open from age 14
Rolling monthly applications

eligibility.en: Individuals aged 14-29 registered in the Batumi municipality.

en: Download the regulation and application form from the programme page
Plan an event in Batumi with budget and timeline
Submit the application to Batumi City Hall in any month
Sign the contract if approved and deliver the project
Submit the programme and financial report

costs.en: Grant of up to 4,000 GEL per project.

score_reason: Rare rolling grant open to teens from 14
